_comment: A metric monitor on how long the API takes to answer. It tells nobody
by itself - rules/api-latency.json is the workflow that does, bound
here by detectorName, the way waitlist-submit-failed.json is.
Why this monitor exists: api-faults.json hears about every request
that throws, and nothing hears about one that succeeds slowly. A D1
query that loses its index, or a fetch to a dependency that starts
hanging, answers 200 every time and raises no issue at all.
WHAT IT COUNTS. Transactions only (is_transaction:true), so p95 is of
whole requests, not of the spans inside them. Two kinds are left out
because they are not requests a person waits on and they move p95 on
their own:
- the */5 cron, which is a scheduled job, runs ~1s, and is 2,015 of
9,569 transactions over the 7 days to 2026-10-27;
- 404s (span.status:not_found), 6,500 of the same 9,569 - scanners
asking for /.env and the like, answered in ~0ms. One burst was
1,371 in an hour, which would drag p95 to zero and hide a real
slowdown behind it.
STATIC, NOT DYNAMIC, for the reason the waitlist monitor gives and a
stronger one: most hours carry 0-10 counted requests, and the daily
p95 over 14 days ranged 20-363ms. Anomaly detection would be learning
noise. 2s over an hour is well clear of anything seen so far, so it
fires on a regression and not on one slow request in a quiet hour -
though at this volume a quiet hour's p95 is close to its max, so a
single request over 2s in an hour with few others CAN open it.
WHAT A DURATION MEANS HERE. A Worker's clock only advances across I/O,
so a request that answers without touching D1 or the network - a 401,
a 404 - reports 0ms however long it really took. p95 is therefore time
spent waiting on I/O, which is exactly what a lost index or a hanging
dependency would inflate, and CPU-bound slowness will not show here.
queryType 1 and events_analytics_platform as in the waitlist monitor;
trace_item_span is the event type for the spans dataset.
The name is how apply.sh finds this detector again, so renaming it in
Sentry means renaming it here and in the rule, or the next run creates
a second one.

detector.name: API slow (production)
detector.description: The API's p95 response time was over 2s for an hour. Slow requests still succeed, so no fault issue is raised for them.
